scope: betangel_research/betfair: Keychain-gated login, delayed-key REST reads, Exchange Stream recorder and one paper-default order gateway; offline tests with injected fakes only

tests.command: BETANGEL_BETFAIR_FORBID_NETWORK=1 BETANGEL_BETFAIR_PROPERTY_SEEDS=300 BETANGEL_BETFAIR_PROPERTY_STEPS=200 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -v
tests.property_command: BETANGEL_BETFAIR_FORBID_NETWORK=1 BETANGEL_BETFAIR_PROPERTY_SEEDS=300 BETANGEL_BETFAIR_PROPERTY_STEPS=200 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_betfair_risk_properties.py -v

limitations: Offline tests with fake transports, sockets, Keychain runners, ttys and clocks; no Betfair endpoint was contacted.
network_calls_made is asserted by the offline test design (block_network, BETANGEL_BETFAIR_FORBID_NETWORK=1 on the recorded command, injected fakes), not measured.
No fact has been checked against the live API; conflicting and unverified facts are handled conservatively and listed in docs/betfair-facts.md.
Property tests check the risk rules only on the generated sequences (300 seeds x 200 steps at integration); they are not proof for every possible sequence.
Python 3.10 compatibility is a syntax check (ast feature_version 3.10), not an executed run.
Paper fills are a conservative model and not execution evidence.

v1 live surface narrowed by Yu's decision D1-D5 (2026-10-10; amendment-v1-live-scope.md in .team-work/betfair-exchange-20261010): live place (LIMIT with LAPSE only), full cancels of our own bets, kill, live-probe (place then cancel), reconciling unknown outcomes and a new hand-typed settle-market. There is no live replace, no live partial cancel, no automatic live settlement (cleared rows never close or settle a live order; the operator settles a CLOSED market and each order is booked at its worst case) and no hedge credit in live risk limits. The kill never takes the gateway lock. F77, settle-market's premise, is inferred; a market Betfair no longer returns cannot be settled in v1 and stays counted at worst case (A20, decided by Yu on 2026-10-11: keep this conservative behaviour and settle soon after close; a possible forget-market only after the first-live T-tests with a fresh design and review, never in v1).
S0 (AGENTS.md, betangel_research/__init__.py, .gitignore, .dockerignore) is not applied; merging to main is blocked until it is.

Astra (Codex) re-review report_ef3fb90d-3ad9-4150-9b50-4796f91a4c32 of the round-4 candidate (checkpoint 43bb3da9), verdict request_changes: two new P2 regressions, no new P1; C1-C4 accepted as closed in the supported production and replay paths (C2's API-layer enforcement accepted; a transport-level guard is optional defence in depth and was not added). R1: concurrent anchor writers (the lock-free kill and a holder) could move the Keychain rollback anchor backwards -> every anchor write goes through credentials.publish_anchor, serialized per profile with the journal head read inside the lock; the kill publishes only in close(), after its sweep. R2: dropping a closed paper market also dropped its chronology barrier -> paper_state schema_version 2 keeps a compact closed-market marker (at most 256, then a floor). Both fixed with regression tests, awaiting Astra's re-review. A20 decided by Yu on 2026-10-11 (collab record report_94134b37-5c9d-4a98-b1de-9bae35a45a37): a market Betfair no longer returns stays counted at worst case; settle soon after close; no forget-market in v1. Details in the report md and brief.md 'Re-review fixes (2026-10-11)'.

R1 follow-up offline review 2026-10-12 (r1-concurrency and r1-liveness lenses; implementer summary, not yet reviewed by Astra): 4 confirmed findings (1 major), all fixed with regression tests: publish_anchor writes only a head that extends the Keychain anchor (a journal restored in place to an older copy under a live session is never anchored: journal_anchor_not_extended), publishes again under a fresh lock when its lock path is replaced during the Keychain write, and only a risk-adding command's open() waits 30 s for another publisher (every other gateway wait is 2 s). Details in the report md and brief.md.

R2 follow-up and its offline review 2026-10-12 (bypass and regressions lenses; implementer summary, not yet reviewed by Astra). The follow-up: a CLOSED book that paper place or replace refuses (validation:V9) or that paper-step ignores now closes its market, journaled in a note before anything else (_note_paper_closed), so a pre-close OPEN book handed in afterwards is refused (paper_market_closed). The review confirmed 4 minor findings (two of them one defect), all addressed, each code fix with a regression test that fails on the tree before it: the marker of a market whose kept book is not CLOSED (its CLOSED book was older than that kept book) is never evicted, so evicting it no longer reopens the market (a resting BACK had filled and settled for 500p after the CLOSED book was seen); a paper gateway journals a paper state only while it still holds its paper lock (_require_paper_lock: paper-step, paper cancel and replace refuse up front, the closed-seen note and every event carrying paper_state check again; gateway_lock_lost, nothing journaled), so a gateway whose .paper.lock was replaced can no longer erase the other gateway's takes or closed markers (place had gained that path with the note; paper-step, cancel and replace's refusal report already had it on base); the report and handoff numbers, stale after the follow-up, come from the rerun of brief steps 4-7. Details in the report md and brief.md.
